hints.content:
### Definition of cosine

For an angle with measure $\theta$ in a right triangle:

$\cos(\theta)=\dfrac{\goldE{\text{adjacent leg length}}}{\purpleD{\text{hypotenuse length}}}$

### Identifying the hypotenuse and the side adjacent to $\angle B$

The side $\goldE{\text{adjacent}}$ to $\angle B$ is $\overline{BC}$ and its length is $\goldE{5}$ units.

The $\purpleD{\text{hypotenuse}}$ is $\overline{AB}$ and its length is $\purpleD{13}$ units.

But $\cos(\beta)$ is the side *adjacent* to $\angle B$ divided by the hypotenuse.

This is the side adjacent to $\angle B$ divided by the side *opposite* to $\angle B$.

But $\cos(\beta)$ is the side adjacent to $\angle B$ divided by the *hypotenuse*.

But $\cos(\beta)$ is the side *adjacent* to $\angle B$ divided by the *hypotenuse*.
